subject: Physics
body: Two balls $A$ and $B$ are placed at the top of a $180\ \text{m}$ tall tower. Ball $A$ is released from the top at $t=0\ \text{s}$. Ball $B$ is thrown vertically downward with an initial velocity $u$ at $t=2\ \text{s}$. After a certain time, both balls meet $100\ \text{m}$ above the ground. Find the value of $u$ in $\text{m s}^{-1}$. [use $g=10\ \text{m s}^{-2}$]
solution: Step 1 — The meeting point is $100\ \text{m}$ above the ground, so each ball has fallen $180-100=80\ \text{m}$. Step 2 — Ball $A$ starts from rest: $80=\dfrac12(10)t^2 \Rightarrow t=4\ \text{s}$. Step 3 — Ball $B$ is released $2\ \text{s}$ later, so it moves for $4-2=2\ \text{s}$: $80 = u(2)+\dfrac12(10)(2)^2 = 2u+20$. Step 4 — Hence $u=30\ \text{m s}^{-1}$.

subject: Physics
body: A body of mass $M$ at rest explodes into three pieces in the ratio of masses $1:1:2$. Two smaller pieces fly off perpendicular to each other with velocities of $30\ \text{m s}^{-1}$ and $40\ \text{m s}^{-1}$ respectively. The velocity of the third piece will be:
solution: Step 1 — The masses are $\dfrac M4,\ \dfrac M4,\ \dfrac M2$. Step 2 — Momenta of the two small pieces: $p_1=\dfrac M4(30)=7.5M$ and $p_2=\dfrac M4(40)=10M$, at right angles, so their resultant is $\sqrt{(7.5M)^2+(10M)^2}=12.5M$. Step 3 — The body was initially at rest, so total momentum stays zero and the third piece carries $12.5M$ in the opposite direction: $\dfrac M2 v=12.5M$. Step 4 — $v=25\ \text{m s}^{-1}$.

subject: Physics
body: The activity of a radioactive material is $2.56\times10^{-3}\ \text{Ci}$. If the half life of the material is $5$ days, after how many days the activity will become $2\times10^{-5}\ \text{Ci}$?
solution: Step 1 — Activity falls by half every half-life, so $\dfrac{A_0}{A}=2^{n}$ where $n$ is the number of half-lives. Step 2 — $\dfrac{A_0}{A}=\dfrac{2.56\times10^{-3}}{2\times10^{-5}}=128=2^7$, so $n=7$. Step 3 — Time $=7\times5=35$ days.

solution:
Step 1 — Rolling without slipping gives $v_{cm}=\omega R$, and the centre of mass moves along the line $y=R$. Step 2 — Angular momentum about $O$ = orbital part + spin part. Orbital: $L_{orb}=m v_{cm}\,R = (1)(\omega R)R=\omega R^2$. Step 3 — Spin about the centre of a thin shell: $L_{spin}=I_{cm}\omega=\dfrac23 mR^2\omega$. Both are clockwise, so they add. Step 4 — $L=\left(1+\dfrac23\right)R^2\omega=\dfrac53R^2\omega$, so $a=5$.

body: A cylinder of fixed capacity of $44.8$ litres contains helium gas at standard temperature and pressure. The amount of heat needed to raise the temperature of the gas in the cylinder by $20.0^\circ\text{C}$ will be: (Given gas constant $R=8.3\ \text{J K}^{-1}\text{mol}^{-1}$)
solution: Step 1 — At STP one mole occupies $22.4$ L, so $n=\dfrac{44.8}{22.4}=2$ mol. Step 2 — The volume is fixed, so heat is supplied at constant volume: $Q=nC_V\Delta T$. Step 3 — Helium is monatomic, $C_V=\dfrac32R$. Step 4 — $Q=2\times\dfrac32\times8.3\times20=498\ \text{J}$.

subject: Physics
body: A wire of length $L$ is hanging from a fixed support. The length changes to $L_1$ and $L_2$ when masses $1\ \text{kg}$ and $2\ \text{kg}$ are suspended respectively from its free end. Then the value of $L$ is equal to:
solution: Step 1 — Within the elastic limit, extension is proportional to the load. Let the extension for $1\ \text{kg}$ be $e$: $L_1-L=e$. Step 2 — For $2\ \text{kg}$ the extension is $2e$: $L_2-L=2e$. Step 3 — Hence $L_2-L=2(L_1-L)$, which gives $L=2L_1-L_2$.

subject: Physics
body:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion A and the other is labelled as Reason R.

Assertion A: The photoelectric effect does not take place, if the energy of the incident radiation is less than the work function of a metal.

Reason R: Kinetic energy of the photoelectrons is zero, if the energy of the incident radiation is equal to the work function of a metal.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below.

options.A: Both A and R are correct and R is the correct explanation of A
options.B: Both A and R are correct but R is not the correct explanation of A
options.C: A is correct but R is not correct
options.D: A is not correct but R is correct

solution:
Step 1 — Einstein's equation: $K_{max}=h
u-\phi$. If $h
u<\phi$ the electron cannot escape the metal, so there is no photoelectric emission; Assertion A is true. Step 2 — If $h
u=\phi$, then $K_{max}=0$; Reason R is also a true statement. Step 3 — However, R describes only the threshold case ($h
u=\phi$). It does not explain why emission is impossible when $h
u<\phi$ (there the electron would need negative kinetic energy). So R is true but not the explanation of A.

subject: Physics
body: A particle of mass $500\ \text{g}$ is moving in a straight line with velocity $v=b\,x^{5/2}$. The work done by the net force during its displacement from $x=0$ to $x=4\ \text{m}$ is: (Take $b=0.25\ \text{m}^{-3/2}\text{s}^{-1}$)
solution: Step 1 — By the work–energy theorem, $W=\Delta K=\dfrac12 m\left(v_f^2-v_i^2\right)$. Step 2 — At $x=0$, $v=0$. At $x=4$: $v=0.25\times4^{5/2}=0.25\times32=8\ \text{m s}^{-1}$. Step 3 — With $m=0.5\ \text{kg}$: $W=\dfrac12(0.5)(8)^2=16\ \text{J}$.

subject: Physics
body: A charged particle moves along a circular path in a uniform magnetic field in a cyclotron. The kinetic energy of the charged particle increases to $4$ times its initial value. What will be the ratio of new radius to the original radius of circular path of the charged particle?
solution: Step 1 — In a magnetic field, $r=\dfrac{mv}{qB}=\dfrac{\sqrt{2mK}}{qB}$, so $r\propto\sqrt K$. Step 2 — With $K'=4K$: $\dfrac{r'}{r}=\sqrt{\dfrac{K'}{K}}=\sqrt4=2$. Step 3 — The ratio is $2:1$.

body: In van der Waals equation $\left[P+\dfrac{a}{V^2}\right][V-b]=RT$; $P$ is pressure, $V$ is volume, $R$ is universal gas constant and $T$ is temperature. The ratio of constants $\dfrac ab$ is dimensionally equal to:
solution: Step 1 — Only quantities of the same dimension can be added, so $\left[\dfrac a{V^2}\right]=[P]\Rightarrow[a]=[PV^2]$. Step 2 — Likewise $[b]=[V]$. Step 3 — $\left[\dfrac ab\right]=\dfrac{[PV^2]}{[V]}=[PV]$.

subject: Physics
body: Two vectors $\vec A$ and $\vec B$ have equal magnitudes. If magnitude of $\vec A+\vec B$ is equal to two times the magnitude of $\vec A-\vec B$, then the angle between $\vec A$ and $\vec B$ will be:
solution: Step 1 — Let $|\vec A|=|\vec B|=a$ and the angle between them be $\theta$. Then $|\vec A+\vec B|^2=2a^2(1+\cos\theta)$ and $|\vec A-\vec B|^2=2a^2(1-\cos\theta)$. Step 2 — Given $|\vec A+\vec B|=2|\vec A-\vec B|$: $1+\cos\theta=4(1-\cos\theta)$. Step 3 — $5\cos\theta=3\Rightarrow\cos\theta=\dfrac35$, so $\theta=\cos^{-1}\left(\dfrac35\right)$.

subject: Physics
body: The escape velocity of a body on a planet $A$ is $12\ \text{km s}^{-1}$. The escape velocity of the body on another planet $B$, whose density is four times and radius is half of the planet $A$, is:
solution: Step 1 — $v_e=\sqrt{\dfrac{2GM}{R}}$ with $M=\dfrac43\pi R^3\rho$, so $v_e=R\sqrt{\dfrac{8\pi G\rho}{3}}\propto R\sqrt\rho$. Step 2 — $\dfrac{v_B}{v_A}=\dfrac{R_B}{R_A}\sqrt{\dfrac{\rho_B}{\rho_A}}=\dfrac12\sqrt4=1$. Step 3 — So $v_B=12\ \text{km s}^{-1}$.

subject: Physics
body: At a certain place the angle of dip is $30^\circ$ and the horizontal component of earth's magnetic field is $0.5\ \text{G}$. The earth's total magnetic field (in G), at that certain place, is:
solution: Step 1 — The horizontal component is $B_H=B\cos\delta$, where $\delta$ is the angle of dip. Step 2 — $B=\dfrac{B_H}{\cos30^\circ}=\dfrac{0.5}{\sqrt3/2}=\dfrac1{\sqrt3}\ \text{G}$.

subject: Physics
body: A longitudinal wave is represented by $x=10\sin2\pi\left(nt-\dfrac x\lambda\right)\ \text{cm}$. The maximum particle velocity will be four times the wave velocity if the determined value of wavelength is equal to:
solution: Step 1 — Amplitude $A=10\ \text{cm}$ and angular frequency $\omega=2\pi n$, so the maximum particle velocity is $v_{p,max}=A\omega=20\pi n$. Step 2 — Wave velocity $v=n\lambda$. Step 3 — Setting $20\pi n=4\,n\lambda$ gives $\lambda=5\pi\ \text{cm}$.

subject: Physics
body: A parallel plate capacitor filled with a medium of dielectric constant $10$, is connected across a battery and is charged. The dielectric slab is replaced by another slab of dielectric constant $15$. Then the energy of capacitor will:
solution: Step 1 — The capacitor stays connected to the battery, so the potential difference $V$ is constant. Step 2 — $C=\dfrac{K\varepsilon_0A}{d}\propto K$, and $U=\dfrac12CV^2\propto K$. Step 3 — $\dfrac{U_2}{U_1}=\dfrac{15}{10}=1.5$, i.e. the energy increases by $50\%$.

subject: Physics
body: A positive charged particle of $100\ \text{mg}$ is thrown in opposite direction to a uniform electric field of strength $1\times10^5\ \text{N C}^{-1}$. If the charge on the particle is $40\ \mu\text{C}$ and the initial velocity is $200\ \text{m s}^{-1}$, how much distance it will travel before coming to rest momentarily?
solution: Step 1 — Electric force $F=qE=(40\times10^{-6})(10^5)=4\ \text{N}$, opposing the motion. Gravity $mg=10^{-4}\times10=10^{-3}\ \text{N}$ is negligible by comparison. Step 2 — Deceleration $a=\dfrac Fm=\dfrac{4}{10^{-4}}=4\times10^4\ \text{m s}^{-2}$. Step 3 — $s=\dfrac{u^2}{2a}=\dfrac{(200)^2}{2\times4\times10^4}=0.5\ \text{m}$.

subject: Physics
body: Using Young's double slit experiment, a monochromatic light of wavelength $5000\ \text{\AA}$ produces fringes of fringe width $0.5\ \text{mm}$. If another monochromatic light of wavelength $6000\ \text{\AA}$ is used and the separation between the slits is doubled, then the new fringe width will be:
solution: Step 1 — Fringe width $\beta=\dfrac{\lambda D}{d}$. Step 2 — New width $\beta'=\beta\cdot\dfrac{\lambda'}{\lambda}\cdot\dfrac{d}{d'}=0.5\times\dfrac{6000}{5000}\times\dfrac12$. Step 3 — $\beta'=0.3\ \text{mm}$.
topic: Interference and Young's double slit experiment

subject: Physics
body: Only $2\%$ of the optical source frequency is the available channel bandwidth for an optical communicating system operating at $1000\ \text{nm}$. If an audio signal requires a bandwidth of $8\ \text{kHz}$, how many channels can be accommodated for transmission:
solution: Step 1 — Source frequency $f=\dfrac c\lambda=\dfrac{3\times10^8}{10^{-6}}=3\times10^{14}\ \text{Hz}$. Step 2 — Available bandwidth $=0.02f=6\times10^{12}\ \text{Hz}$. Step 3 — Number of channels $=\dfrac{6\times10^{12}}{8\times10^{3}}=7.5\times10^8=75\times10^7$.
topic: Bandwidth of signals and transmission media

subject: Physics
body: Two coils require $20$ minutes and $60$ minutes respectively to produce same amount of heat energy when connected separately to the same source. If they are connected in parallel arrangement to the same source; the time required to produce same amount of heat by the combination of coils, will be ______ min.
solution: Step 1 — Heat $H=\dfrac{V^2}{R}t$ for the same $V$ and same $H$, so $t\propto R$. Thus $R_1:R_2=20:60$. Step 2 — In parallel, $R_p=\dfrac{R_1R_2}{R_1+R_2}$, so the time taken is $t_p=\dfrac{t_1t_2}{t_1+t_2}$. Step 3 — $t_p=\dfrac{20\times60}{20+60}=15\ \text{min}$.

subject: Physics
body: The intensity of the light from a bulb incident on a surface is $0.22\ \text{W m}^{-2}$. The amplitude of the magnetic field in this light-wave is ______ $\times10^{-9}\ \text{T}$. (Given: Permittivity of vacuum $\epsilon_0=8.85\times10^{-12}\ \text{C}^2\text{N}^{-1}\text{m}^{-2}$, speed of light in vacuum $c=3\times10^8\ \text{m s}^{-1}$)
solution: Step 1 — Intensity of an EM wave: $I=\dfrac12\epsilon_0cE_0^2$, and $E_0=cB_0$, so $I=\dfrac12\epsilon_0c^3B_0^2$. Step 2 — $B_0=\sqrt{\dfrac{2I}{\epsilon_0c^3}}=\sqrt{\dfrac{0.44}{(8.85\times10^{-12})(27\times10^{24})}}$. Step 3 — $B_0=\sqrt{1.84\times10^{-15}}\approx4.29\times10^{-8}\ \text{T}=42.9\times10^{-9}\ \text{T}$, i.e. $\approx43$.

body: A body is performing simple harmonic motion with an amplitude of $10\ \text{cm}$. The velocity of the body was tripled by an air jet when it is at $5\ \text{cm}$ from its mean position. The new amplitude of vibration is $\sqrt x\ \text{cm}$. The value of $x$ is ______.
solution: Step 1 — The angular frequency $\omega$ depends only on the mass and the restoring constant, so it is unchanged. Step 2 — Before the jet, at $x=5\ \text{cm}$: $v^2=\omega^2(A^2-x^2)=\omega^2(100-25)=75\omega^2$. Step 3 — After the jet the speed is $3v$ at the same position: $9(75\omega^2)=\omega^2(A'^2-25)$. Step 4 — $A'^2=675+25=700$, so $x=700$.

body: $300\ \text{cal}$ of heat is given to a heat engine and it rejects $225\ \text{cal}$ of heat. If source temperature is $227^\circ\text{C}$, then the temperature of sink will be ______ $^\circ\text{C}$.
solution: Step 1 — For the (ideal) engine, $\dfrac{Q_2}{Q_1}=\dfrac{T_2}{T_1}$. Step 2 — $T_1=227+273=500\ \text{K}$, so $T_2=500\times\dfrac{225}{300}=375\ \text{K}$. Step 3 — In Celsius: $375-273=102^\circ\text{C}$.

body: $\sqrt{d_1}$ and $\sqrt{d_2}$ are the impact parameters corresponding to scattering angles $60^\circ$ and $90^\circ$ respectively, when an $\alpha$ particle is approaching a gold nucleus. For $d_1=x\,d_2$, the value of $x$ will be ______.
solution: Step 1 — In Rutherford scattering the impact parameter is $b=\dfrac{kZe^2}{K}\cot\dfrac\theta2\ \Rightarrow\ b\propto\cot\dfrac\theta2$. Step 2 — $\dfrac{\sqrt{d_1}}{\sqrt{d_2}}=\dfrac{\cot30^\circ}{\cot45^\circ}=\dfrac{\sqrt3}{1}$. Step 3 — Squaring, $d_1=3d_2$, so $x=3$.

body: A transistor is used in an amplifier circuit in common emitter mode. If the base current changes by $100\ \mu\text{A}$, it brings a change of $10\ \text{mA}$ in collector current. If the load resistance is $2\ \text{k}\Omega$ and input resistance is $1\ \text{k}\Omega$, the value of power gain is $x\times10^4$. The value of $x$ is ______.
solution: Step 1 — Current gain $\beta=\dfrac{\Delta I_C}{\Delta I_B}=\dfrac{10\ \text{mA}}{100\ \mu\text{A}}=100$. Step 2 — Voltage gain $A_V=\beta\dfrac{R_L}{R_{in}}=100\times\dfrac{2}{1}=200$. Step 3 — Power gain $=\beta A_V=100\times200=2\times10^4$, so $x=2$.

subject: Physics
body: A parallel beam of light is allowed to fall on a transparent spherical globe of diameter $30\ \text{cm}$ and refractive index $1.5$. The distance from the centre of the globe at which the beam of light can converge is ______ mm.
solution: Step 1 — Radius $R=15\ \text{cm}$. Refraction at the first surface (object at infinity): $\dfrac{1.5}{v}=\dfrac{1.5-1}{R}\Rightarrow v=3R=45\ \text{cm}$ from the first pole. Step 2 — This image lies $45-30=15\ \text{cm}$ beyond the second surface, so it acts as a virtual object for it ($u=+15\ \text{cm}$). Step 3 — Second surface ($R_2=-15\ \text{cm}$, glass to air): $\dfrac1v-\dfrac{1.5}{15}=\dfrac{1-1.5}{-15}=\dfrac1{30}\Rightarrow\dfrac1v=\dfrac4{30}$, so $v=7.5\ \text{cm}$ from the second pole. Step 4 — Distance from the centre $=15+7.5=22.5\ \text{cm}=225\ \text{mm}$.

body:
Production of iron in blast furnace follows the following equation
$\mathrm{Fe_3O_4(s)+4CO(g)\rightarrow3Fe(l)+4CO_2(g)}$
when $4.640\ \text{kg}$ of $\mathrm{Fe_3O_4}$ and $2.520\ \text{kg}$ of $\mathrm{CO}$ are allowed to react then the amount of iron (in g) produced is:
[Given: Molar atomic mass ($\text{g mol}^{-1}$): Fe = 56, O = 16, C = 12]
solution: Step 1 — Molar mass of $\mathrm{Fe_3O_4}=3(56)+4(16)=232\ \text{g mol}^{-1}$, so $n=\dfrac{4640}{232}=20$ mol. Molar mass of $\mathrm{CO}=28$, so $n=\dfrac{2520}{28}=90$ mol. Step 2 — The equation needs $4$ mol CO per mol $\mathrm{Fe_3O_4}$: $20$ mol of $\mathrm{Fe_3O_4}$ requires $80$ mol CO, and $90$ mol is available, so $\mathrm{Fe_3O_4}$ is the limiting reagent. Step 3 — Fe produced $=3\times20=60$ mol, i.e. $60\times56=3360\ \text{g}$.

subject: Chemistry
body:
Which of the following statements are correct?
(A) The electronic configuration of Cr is $[\mathrm{Ar}]3d^54s^1$.
(B) The magnetic quantum number may have a negative value.
(C) In the ground state of an atom, the orbitals are filled in order of their increasing energies.
(D) The total number of nodes are given by $n-2$.

Choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
solution: Step 1 — (A) is correct: Cr takes $3d^54s^1$ because a half-filled $d$ subshell is extra stable. Step 2 — (B) is correct: $m_l$ takes values $-l,\dots,0,\dots,+l$, which include negative integers. Step 3 — (C) is correct: the Aufbau principle fills orbitals in increasing order of energy. Step 4 — (D) is wrong: radial nodes $=n-l-1$ and angular nodes $=l$, so total nodes $=n-1$, not $n-2$. Hence (A), (B) and (C) only.

subject: Chemistry
body:
Arrange the following in the decreasing order of their covalent character:
(A) LiCl
(B) NaCl
(C) KCl
(D) CsCl

Choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
solution: Step 1 — By Fajans' rules, a smaller cation has greater polarising power and so distorts the anion's electron cloud more, increasing covalent character. Step 2 — Cation size increases down the group: $\mathrm{Li^+}<\mathrm{Na^+}<\mathrm{K^+}<\mathrm{Cs^+}$. Step 3 — Covalent character therefore decreases in the order $\mathrm{LiCl}>\mathrm{NaCl}>\mathrm{KCl}>\mathrm{CsCl}$, i.e. (A) > (B) > (C) > (D).
topic: Fajans' rules (covalent character of ionic bonds)

subject: Chemistry
body: The solubility of $\mathrm{AgCl}$ will be maximum in which of the following?
solution: Step 1 — $\mathrm{AgCl(s)\rightleftharpoons Ag^+ + Cl^-}$ with $K_{sp}=[\mathrm{Ag^+}][\mathrm{Cl^-}]$. Step 2 — $\mathrm{KCl}$ and $\mathrm{HCl}$ add $\mathrm{Cl^-}$, and $\mathrm{AgNO_3}$ adds $\mathrm{Ag^+}$; by the common-ion effect each of these shifts the equilibrium to the left and lowers the solubility. Step 3 — Deionised water has no common ion, so the solubility ($\sqrt{K_{sp}}$) is highest there.

subject: Chemistry
body: Which of the following is a correct statement?

options.B: Any amount of dispersed phase can be added to emulsion without destabilising it.
options.C: Mixing two oppositely charged sols in equal amount neutralises charges and stabilises colloids.
options.D: Presence of equal and similar charges on colloidal particles provides stability to the colloidal solution.

solution: Step 1 — Brownian motion keeps the particles moving and prevents them from settling, so it helps stability; the first statement is wrong. Step 2 — Adding too much dispersed phase breaks an emulsion; the second statement is wrong. Step 3 — Mixing oppositely charged sols neutralises the charges and makes the sols coagulate (destabilises them); the third statement is wrong. Step 4 — Particles carrying the same charge repel one another and do not aggregate, which stabilises the sol; the fourth statement is correct.

subject: Chemistry
body: The electronic configuration of $\mathrm{Pt}$ (atomic number $78$) is:
solution: Step 1 — Xenon has $54$ electrons, leaving $78-54=24$ electrons to place: $4f^{14}$ plus $10$ more in $5d/6s$. Step 2 — Platinum is an exception to Madelung's order: the observed ground state is $5d^96s^1$ (a nearly filled $5d$ with a single $6s$ electron is lower in energy than $5d^86s^2$). Step 3 — Option B uses a krypton core ($36+14+10=60\neq78$), option C is $5d^{10}6s^0$ (palladium-like), and option D is the unmodified Madelung filling. The correct choice is $[\mathrm{Xe}]4f^{14}5d^96s^1$.

subject: Chemistry
body: In isolation of which one of the following metals from their ores, the use of cyanide salt is not commonly involved?
solution: Step 1 — Gold and silver ores are leached with a dilute $\mathrm{NaCN}$ solution (the MacArthur–Forrest process), forming $[\mathrm{Au(CN)_2}]^-$ and $[\mathrm{Ag(CN)_2}]^-$, from which the metal is displaced with zinc. Step 2 — Cyanide-based reagents are also used in processing of copper sulphide ores. Step 3 — Zinc is obtained by roasting $\mathrm{ZnS}$ to $\mathrm{ZnO}$ and reducing it with carbon (or by electrolysis); no cyanide leaching step is involved, so zinc is the answer.
chapter: General Principles and Processes of Isolation of Elements

subject: Chemistry
body: Which one of the following reactions indicates the reducing ability of hydrogen peroxide in basic medium?
solution: Step 1 — $\mathrm{H_2O_2}$ acts as a reducing agent when it is itself oxidised, i.e. when it is converted to $\mathrm{O_2}$. Step 2 — Reaction B and D oxidise a substance ($\mathrm{PbS}\to\mathrm{PbSO_4}$, $\mathrm{Mn^{2+}}\to\mathrm{Mn^{4+}}$), so $\mathrm{H_2O_2}$ is the oxidant there. Step 3 — Reaction A does show $\mathrm{H_2O_2}\to\mathrm{O_2}$, but it produces $\mathrm{H_3O^+}$, i.e. it occurs in acidic medium. Step 4 — In reaction C, $\mathrm{MnO_4^-}$ is reduced to $\mathrm{MnO_2}$, $\mathrm{H_2O_2}$ is oxidised to $\mathrm{O_2}$, and $\mathrm{OH^-}$ is produced, which indicates a basic medium. So C is correct.

List - I (Metal) | List - II (Application)
(A) Cs | (I) High temperature thermometer
(B) Ga | (II) Water repellent sprays
(C) B | (III) Photoelectric cells
(D) Si | (IV) Bullet proof vest

Choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
solution: Step 1 — Caesium has a very low ionisation energy and emits electrons readily on exposure to light, so it is used in photoelectric cells (A–III). Step 2 — Gallium stays liquid over a very wide temperature range, which suits high-temperature thermometers (B–I). Step 3 — Boron fibres and boron carbide are used in bullet-proof vests (C–IV). Step 4 — Organosilicon polymers (silicones) are used in water-repellent sprays (D–II).

subject: Chemistry
body: The oxoacid of phosphorus that is easily obtained from a reaction of alkali and white phosphorus and has two $\mathrm{P{-}H}$ bonds, is:
solution: Step 1 — White phosphorus reacts with hot aqueous alkali: $\mathrm{P_4+3NaOH+3H_2O\rightarrow PH_3+3NaH_2PO_2}$. The salt formed is sodium hypophosphite, whose parent acid is $\mathrm{H_3PO_2}$ (phosphinic acid). Step 2 — The structure of $\mathrm{H_3PO_2}$ is $\mathrm{H_2P(O)OH}$: two $\mathrm{P{-}H}$ bonds, one $\mathrm{P{-}OH}$ and one $\mathrm{P{=}O}$. Step 3 — Phosphonic acid ($\mathrm{H_3PO_3}$) has one $\mathrm{P{-}H}$ bond, and hypophosphoric acid ($\mathrm{H_4P_2O_6}$) has none; pyrophosphorus acid is not formed directly from $\mathrm{P_4}$ and alkali. So the answer is phosphinic acid.

subject: Chemistry
body: The acid that is believed to be mainly responsible for the damage of Taj Mahal is
solution: Step 1 — Industrial emissions of $\mathrm{SO_2}$ (for example from nearby refineries) are oxidised in the air and dissolve in rain as $\mathrm{H_2SO_4}$, causing acid rain. Step 2 — The marble of the monument, $\mathrm{CaCO_3}$, is attacked: $\mathrm{CaCO_3+H_2SO_4\rightarrow CaSO_4+H_2O+CO_2}$. This corrodes and discolours the surface (marble cancer). Hence sulfuric acid.

subject: Chemistry
body: Two isomers $A$ and $B$ with molecular formula $\mathrm{C_4H_8}$ give different products on oxidation with $\mathrm{KMnO_4}$ in acidic medium. Isomer $A$ on reaction with $\mathrm{KMnO_4/H^+}$ results in effervescence of a gas and gives ketone. The compound $A$ is
solution: Step 1 — Effervescence means $\mathrm{CO_2}$ is released, which happens when the terminal $\mathrm{=CH_2}$ group is oxidised. So $A$ must be a terminal alkene: but-1-ene or 2-methylpropene. Step 2 — But-1-ene gives $\mathrm{CH_3CH_2COOH}+\mathrm{CO_2}$ (a carboxylic acid, not a ketone). Step 3 — 2-Methylpropene, $\mathrm{(CH_3)_2C=CH_2}$, gives $\mathrm{(CH_3)_2C=O}$ (acetone, a ketone) $+\ \mathrm{CO_2}$. Step 4 — The but-2-enes give two molecules of $\mathrm{CH_3COOH}$ and no gas. So $A$ is 2-methylpropene.

Step 1 — $\mathrm{(CH_3)_3CLi}$ is both a very strong base and a reagent for lithium–halogen exchange. Step 2 — The first equivalent removes the most acidic proton, the phenolic $\mathrm{O{-}H}$, giving the lithium phenoxide $\mathrm{Ar{-}OLi}$. Step 3 — A second equivalent replaces $\mathrm{Br}$ by $\mathrm{Li}$ (halogen–metal exchange), so $A$ has both $\mathrm{Li}$ on the ring carbon and $\mathrm{OLi}$. Step 4 — The aryl-lithium attacks $\mathrm{CO_2}$ to give a carboxylate, and $\mathrm{H_3O^+}$ protonates both the carboxylate and the phenoxide, giving salicylic acid (2-hydroxybenzoic acid). Option A would leave the acidic $\mathrm{OH}$ intact, which cannot survive an organolithium; options C and D are not formed under these conditions.

body:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: The esterification of carboxylic acid with an alcohol is a nucleophilic acyl substitution.

Statement II: Electron withdrawing groups in the carboxylic acid will increase the rate of esterification reaction.

Choose the most appropriate option:

options.A: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
options.B: Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
options.C: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
options.D: Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.

solution: Step 1 — Statement I: in Fischer esterification the alcohol (nucleophile) attacks the carbonyl carbon of the protonated acid to form a tetrahedral intermediate; loss of water then regenerates the carbonyl. The $\mathrm{OH}$ group of the acid is replaced by $\mathrm{OR}$, so it is a nucleophilic acyl substitution; Statement I is correct. Step 2 — Statement II: an electron-withdrawing group makes the carbonyl carbon more electrophilic, so the attack by the alcohol is faster, and it also stabilises the tetrahedral intermediate. The rate of esterification therefore increases; Statement II is correct. Both statements are correct.

Step 1 — Reaction for $A$: the $\mathrm{-NH_2}$ group strongly activates the ring towards ortho/para substitution. With excess bromine water all three activated positions are brominated, giving $2,4,6$-tribromoaniline (white precipitate). Step 2 — Reaction for $B$: acetylation converts $\mathrm{-NH_2}$ to $\mathrm{-NHCOCH_3}$, which is a weaker activator and bulkier, so bromination in acetic acid stops at one $\mathrm{Br}$, mainly at the para position. Step 3 — Hydrolysis with $\mathrm{HCl}$ removes the acetyl group and gives $4$-bromoaniline. So $A$ = tribromoaniline and $B$ = $4$-bromoaniline.

body: The polymer, which can be stretched and retains its original status on releasing the force is
solution: Step 1 — A polymer that can be stretched and returns to its original shape is an elastomer, which has weak intermolecular forces and coiled chains. Step 2 — Buna-N (a copolymer of buta-1,3-diene and acrylonitrile) is a synthetic rubber, i.e. an elastomer. Step 3 — Bakelite is a rigid thermosetting polymer, while nylon 6,6 and terylene are fibres with strong hydrogen bonding or dipole interactions that resist stretching.

body: Sugar moiety in DNA and RNA molecules respectively are
solution: Step 1 — DNA (deoxyribonucleic acid) contains $\beta$-D-2-deoxyribose, which lacks the $\mathrm{OH}$ group on carbon-2. Step 2 — RNA (ribonucleic acid) contains $\beta$-D-ribose, which has an $\mathrm{OH}$ on carbon-2. Step 3 — The order DNA, RNA is therefore $\beta$-D-2-deoxyribose, $\beta$-D-ribose.

body: Which of the following compounds does not contain sulfur atom?
solution: Step 1 — Cimetidine contains a thioether linkage ($\mathrm{-CH_2-S-CH_2-}$) and ranitidine also contains a thioether ($\mathrm{-S-}$) link. Step 2 — Saccharin (benzoic sulfimide, $\mathrm{C_7H_5NO_3S}$) has a sulfonyl group. Step 3 — Histamine, $\mathrm{C_5H_9N_3}$, is 2-(imidazol-4-yl)ethanamine and contains only C, H and N, so it has no sulfur.

body:
Given below are two statements.

Statement I: Phenols are weakly acidic.

Statement II: Therefore they are freely soluble in NaOH solution and are weaker acids than alcohols and water.

Choose the most appropriate option:

options.A: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
options.B: Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
options.C: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
options.D: Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.

solution: Step 1 — Statement I is correct: phenol has $pK_a\approx10$, so it is only weakly acidic and dissolves in $\mathrm{NaOH}$ as sodium phenoxide. Step 2 — Statement II claims phenols are weaker acids than alcohols and water. This is false: the phenoxide ion is stabilised by resonance with the ring, so phenol ($pK_a\approx10$) is a stronger acid than water ($pK_a\approx15.7$) and alcohols ($pK_a\approx16$–$18$). Step 3 — Statement I is correct and Statement II is incorrect.

body: Geraniol, a volatile organic compound, is a component of rose oil. The density of the vapour is $0.46\ \text{g L}^{-1}$ at $257^\circ\text{C}$ and $100\ \text{mm Hg}$. The molar mass of geraniol is ______ $\text{g mol}^{-1}$. (Nearest integer) [Given: $R=0.082\ \text{L atm K}^{-1}\text{mol}^{-1}$]
solution: Step 1 — From $PV=\dfrac mMRT$ we get $M=\dfrac{dRT}{P}$ where $d$ is the density. Step 2 — $T=257+273=530\ \text{K}$ and $P=\dfrac{100}{760}=0.1316\ \text{atm}$. Step 3 — $M=\dfrac{0.46\times0.082\times530}{0.1316}=\dfrac{19.99}{0.1316}\approx151.9\approx152\ \text{g mol}^{-1}$.

solution: Step 1 — Molar mass of $\mathrm{NH_3}=17\ \text{g mol}^{-1}$, so $85\ \text{g}=\dfrac{85}{17}=5$ mol. Step 2 — Enthalpy change $=5\times23.4=117\ \text{kJ}$.

body: $1.2\ \text{mL}$ of acetic acid is dissolved in water to make $2.0\ \text{L}$ of solution. The depression in freezing point observed for this strength of acid is $0.0198^\circ\text{C}$. The percentage of dissociation of the acid is ______. (Nearest integer) [Given: Density of acetic acid is $1.02\ \text{g mL}^{-1}$; Molar mass of acetic acid is $60\ \text{g mol}^{-1}$; $K_f(\mathrm{H_2O})=1.85\ \text{K kg mol}^{-1}$]
solution: Step 1 — Mass of acid $=1.2\times1.02=1.224\ \text{g}$, so moles $=\dfrac{1.224}{60}=0.0204$ mol in $2.0\ \text{L}$. For such a dilute aqueous solution, take $2.0\ \text{L}\approx2.0\ \text{kg}$ of water, so $m\approx0.0102\ \text{mol kg}^{-1}$. Step 2 — $\Delta T_f=i\,K_f\,m\Rightarrow i=\dfrac{0.0198}{1.85\times0.0102}=1.049$. Step 3 — For $\mathrm{CH_3COOH\rightleftharpoons CH_3COO^-+H^+}$, $i=1+\alpha$, so $\alpha=0.049$. Step 4 — Percentage dissociation $\approx4.9\%\approx5$.

body: A dilute solution of sulphuric acid is electrolysed using a current of $0.10\ \text{A}$ for $2$ hours to produce hydrogen and oxygen gas. The total volume of gases produced at STP is ______ $\text{cm}^3$. (Nearest integer) [Given: Faraday constant $F=96500\ \text{C mol}^{-1}$ at STP, molar volume of an ideal gas is $22.7\ \text{L mol}^{-1}$]
solution: Step 1 — Charge passed $Q=It=0.10\times7200=720\ \text{C}$, so moles of electrons $=\dfrac{720}{96500}=7.46\times10^{-3}$ mol. Step 2 — Cathode: $2\mathrm{H^+}+2e^-\rightarrow\mathrm{H_2}$, so $n(\mathrm{H_2})=\dfrac{7.46\times10^{-3}}{2}=3.73\times10^{-3}$ mol. Anode: $2\mathrm{H_2O}\rightarrow\mathrm{O_2}+4\mathrm{H^+}+4e^-$, so $n(\mathrm{O_2})=\dfrac{7.46\times10^{-3}}{4}=1.865\times10^{-3}$ mol. Step 3 — Total gas $=5.596\times10^{-3}$ mol, so $V=5.596\times10^{-3}\times22.7\ \text{L}=0.127\ \text{L}=127\ \text{cm}^3$.

subject: Chemistry
body: The activation energy of one of the reactions in a biochemical process is $532611\ \text{J mol}^{-1}$. When the temperature falls from $310\ \text{K}$ to $300\ \text{K}$, the change in rate constant observed is $k_{300}=x\times10^{-3}\,k_{310}$. The value of $x$ is ______. [Given: $\ln10=2.3$, $R=8.3\ \text{J K}^{-1}\text{mol}^{-1}$]
solution: Step 1 — Arrhenius equation: $\ln\dfrac{k_{300}}{k_{310}}=-\dfrac{E_a}{R}\left(\dfrac1{300}-\dfrac1{310}\right)$. Step 2 — $\dfrac{E_a}{R}=\dfrac{532611}{8.3}=64170$ and $\dfrac1{300}-\dfrac1{310}=\dfrac{10}{93000}=1.0753\times10^{-4}$. Step 3 — The product is $6.9$, so $\ln\dfrac{k_{300}}{k_{310}}=-6.9=-3\ln10$. Step 4 — $\dfrac{k_{300}}{k_{310}}=10^{-3}$, so $x=1$.

The number of terminal oxygen atoms present in the product $B$ obtained from the following reaction is ______.
$\mathrm{FeCr_2O_4+Na_2CO_3+O_2\rightarrow A+Fe_2O_3+CO_2}$
$\mathrm{A+H^+\rightarrow B+H_2O+Na^+}$
solution: Step 1 — Fusion of chromite ore with sodium carbonate in air gives sodium chromate: $A=\mathrm{Na_2CrO_4}$. Step 2 — Acidification converts chromate into dichromate: $2\mathrm{CrO_4^{2-}}+2\mathrm{H^+}\rightarrow\mathrm{Cr_2O_7^{2-}}+\mathrm{H_2O}$, so $B$ is the dichromate ion. Step 3 — $\mathrm{Cr_2O_7^{2-}}$ is $[\mathrm{O_3Cr{-}O{-}CrO_3}]^{2-}$: each chromium carries $3$ terminal oxygens and one oxygen bridges the two chromium atoms. Terminal oxygens $=3+3=6$.

subject: Chemistry
body: An acidified manganate solution undergoes disproportionation reaction. The spin-only magnetic moment value of the product having manganese in higher oxidation state is ______ B.M. (Nearest integer)
solution: Step 1 — In acid, manganate disproportionates: $3\mathrm{MnO_4^{2-}}+4\mathrm{H^+}\rightarrow2\mathrm{MnO_4^-}+\mathrm{MnO_2}+2\mathrm{H_2O}$. Step 2 — Manganese is $+6$ in manganate, and goes to $+7$ in permanganate and $+4$ in $\mathrm{MnO_2}$. The higher oxidation state product is $\mathrm{MnO_4^-}$. Step 3 — $\mathrm{Mn^{7+}}$ has the configuration $[\mathrm{Ar}]3d^0$, so there are no unpaired electrons. Step 4 — $\mu=\sqrt{n(n+2)}=0$ B.M.

body: Kjeldahl's method was used for the estimation of nitrogen in an organic compound. The ammonia evolved from $0.55\ \text{g}$ of the compound neutralised $12.5\ \text{mL}$ of $1\ \text{M}\ \mathrm{H_2SO_4}$ solution. The percentage of nitrogen in the compound is ______. (Nearest integer)
solution: Step 1 — Moles of $\mathrm{H_2SO_4}=12.5\times10^{-3}\times1=12.5\times10^{-3}$ mol. Step 2 — $2\mathrm{NH_3}+\mathrm{H_2SO_4}\rightarrow(\mathrm{NH_4})_2\mathrm{SO_4}$, so moles of $\mathrm{NH_3}=2\times12.5\times10^{-3}=25\times10^{-3}$ mol, and the same number of moles of nitrogen. Step 3 — Mass of $\mathrm{N}=25\times10^{-3}\times14=0.35\ \text{g}$. Step 4 — $\%\,\mathrm{N}=\dfrac{0.35}{0.55}\times100=63.6\approx64$.

The total number of structures/compounds which possess asymmetric carbon atoms is ______.
solution:
Step 1 — An asymmetric (chiral) carbon is bonded to four different groups. Step 2 — 2-Chlorobutane: $\mathrm{C_2}$ carries $\mathrm{H}$, $\mathrm{Cl}$, $\mathrm{CH_3}$ and $\mathrm{C_2H_5}$, so it is chiral. Glycine, $\mathrm{H_2N{-}CH_2{-}COOH}$: the $\mathrm{CH_2}$ carbon has two identical hydrogens, so it has none. Alanine: the $\alpha$-carbon carries $\mathrm{H}$, $\mathrm{NH_2}$, $\mathrm{CH_3}$ and $\mathrm{COOH}$, so it is chiral. Styrene has no $sp^3$ carbon with four different groups. Menthol: the ring carbons bearing $\mathrm{OH}$, isopropyl and methyl each have four different groups around them, so it has three asymmetric carbons. Step 3 — Compounds with asymmetric carbons: 2-chlorobutane, alanine and menthol, a total of $3$.

$\mathrm{C_6H_{12}O_6\xrightarrow{Zymase}A\xrightarrow[\Delta]{NaOI}B+CHI_3}$
The number of carbon atoms present in the product $B$ is ______.
solution: Step 1 — Zymase (an enzyme from yeast) ferments glucose: $\mathrm{C_6H_{12}O_6\rightarrow2C_2H_5OH+2CO_2}$, so $A=\mathrm{C_2H_5OH}$. Step 2 — Ethanol contains the $\mathrm{CH_3CH(OH){-}}$ unit, so it gives the iodoform test with $\mathrm{NaOI}$: $\mathrm{C_2H_5OH+4I_2+6NaOH\rightarrow CHI_3+HCOONa+5NaI+5H_2O}$. Step 3 — $B=\mathrm{HCOONa}$ (sodium formate), which contains $1$ carbon atom.
